## Root Cause

The drain is permanently blocked by the ZooKeeper PodDisruptionBudget (PDB), but the underlying trigger is that **`zk-2` is already unhealthy** (CrashLoopBackOff, 37 restarts), not the drain itself.

### Evidence

| Pod   | Node                        | Status            | Ready |
|-------|-----------------------------|-------------------|-------|
| zk-0  | ip-10-0-81-17 (**draining**) | Running           | ✅    |
| zk-1  | ip-10-0-82-54               | Running           | ✅    |
| zk-2  | ip-10-0-83-91               | CrashLoopBackOff  | ❌    |

`zk-2` logs show a fatal ZooKeeper epoch mismatch:
```
ERROR: Unable to load database on disk
java.io.IOException: The accepted epoch, 7 is less than the current epoch, 8
```

### Why the drain is stuck

The ZooKeeper PDB is configured with `minAvailable: 2` (matching `app: zookeeper` labels) [cite: tasks/run-application/configure-pdb#specifying-a-poddisruptionbudget-3]. With `zk-2` already not Ready, the PDB sees only **2 healthy pods** (`zk-0` and `zk-1`). Evicting `zk-0` would drop healthy replicas to 1, violating `minAvailable: 2`. As documented, when evicting a pod would violate the budget, the drain retries indefinitely and will never complete on its own [cite: tasks/run-application/configure-pdb#specifying-a-poddisruptionbudget-3][cite: concepts/workloads/pods/disruptions#pod-disruption-budgets-1].

### Why --disable-eviction or force delete are NOT safe here

**Do not** use `--disable-eviction` or `kubectl delete --force` on `zk-0` right now. ZooKeeper requires a quorum of ≥ 2 out of 3 nodes. `zk-2` is already down; removing `zk-0` as well would leave only `zk-1`, **breaking ZooKeeper quorum and taking down all Kafka brokers** that depend on it. Force-deleting a StatefulSet pod also carries the risk of split-brain in quorum-based systems [cite: tasks/run-application/force-delete-stateful-set-pod#statefulset-considerations-1].

### Fix (perform in this order)

1. **Fix `zk-2` first.** The epoch error (`accepted epoch 7 < current epoch 8`) means `zk-2`'s data directory is stale. The standard ZooKeeper remediation is to delete the contents of the data volume for `zk-2` so it can re-join the ensemble and resync from the leader. Coordinate with your Kafka/ZooKeeper team on the exact procedure for your setup (e.g., deleting the `version-2/` directory on the PV and restarting the pod).

2. **Wait for `zk-2` to become Ready.** Once all three ZK pods are healthy, the PDB will have 3 healthy replicas and will allow one voluntary disruption — satisfying `minAvailable: 2` even after `zk-0` is evicted.

3. **The drain will then complete automatically** (it is already running and retrying every 5 s), or you can re-run it. No flags need to change.

If the patch window closes before `zk-2` is fixed, the safest course is to **uncordon `ip-10-0-81-17`** (`kubectl uncordon ip-10-0-81-17`) and reschedule the maintenance window. This is preferable to risking a ZooKeeper quorum loss during production hours.
